answers.Q1: Eight volumes are listed, though the register preserves nine entries because one ledger appears twice.
answers.Q2: Cart 2 delivered the largest number, four volumes; cart 1 and cart 3 each carried two.
answers.Q3: The clerk attached a plain buff cross-reference slip, not a new shelf label, when one volume bore another volume's shelf reference.
answers.Q4: T. Fenwick, the borough porter, unloaded cart 3; the note does not credit a second person.
answers.Q5: Lena Brice of conservation supplied the narrow green bands; they were not taken from the reading-room stock.
answers.Q6: Two volumes remained in the review cabinet; the others had been cleared to the returned-ledger shelves.
